# actibase Package

`actibase` is a baseline package for raw actigraphy and activity
workflows. It provides readers and core preprocessing helpers that
downstream packages can build on, such as step-count or summarization
overlays.

## Installation

You can install `actibase` from GitHub with:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jhuwit/actibase")
```

## Quick start

``` r

library(actibase)
res = acti_standardize_data(acti_raw_data)
resampled = acti_resample(res, sample_rate = 30L)
```

## What lives here

`actibase` keeps the primitives that other packages can build on:

- accelerometer column standardization and axis reshaping, including
  common `x/y/z`, `acc_*`, and `acceleration_*` input names
- timestamp-aware resampling to a sampling rate or requested timestamps
- time-of-day, date, day-boundary, and interval helpers
- sample-rate and device-range metadata lookup
- raw-sample QC flags and CDC NHANES letter labels for comparing
  raw-data checks with NHANES output
- day-inclusion summaries and basic zero handling

Device-limit helpers distinguish adjacent samples from sustained runs:
[`acti_flag_adjacent_device_limit_samples()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
marks near-limit samples with a neighboring limit sample, while
[`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs.md)
marks axis- and sign-specific runs meeting `min_length`. The older
function names remain available for compatibility.

The flag functions label questionable raw samples and intervals; they do
not replace vendor readers, wear/nonwear algorithms, or activity
summaries.
[`acti_flag_cdc_labels()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_cdc_labels.md)
is syntactic sugar for attaching CDC letter codes to flag columns
already computed, so raw-data checks can be compared with NHANES.

Higher-level summarization, step-count mapping, and downstream analysis
should live in overlay packages.

## NHANES PAM flag mapping

The table maps the CDC NHANES PAM minute flags to the general-purpose
sample-level or window-level helpers in `actibase`. The functions do not
reproduce CDC’s data pipeline automatically: use the CDC thresholds and
window rules when matching NHANES output. Flags with axis-specific
output need `by_axis = TRUE` where that option is available.
[`acti_flag_cdc_labels()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_cdc_labels.md)
can combine the resulting logical columns into CDC-style letter strings.

| CDC code | CDC definition (summary) | `actibase` function and output | Match notes |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| A–C | Axis-specific spikes: adjacent-sample change ≥11 g | `acti_flag_spike(by_axis = TRUE)`: `flag_spike_X/Y/Z` | Sample-level; set `spike_size = 11` and use the appropriate sampling rate. |
| D–F | Per-minute count of positive near-limit values, ≥690 samples | [`acti_flag_device_limit_windows()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_device_limit_windows.md): `flag_device_max_X/Y/Z` | Set `min_count = 690`, `window_seconds = 60`, `dynamic_range = c(-6, 6)`, and `epsilon = 0.05`. |
| G–I | Per-minute count of negative near-limit values, ≥690 samples | [`acti_flag_device_limit_windows()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_device_limit_windows.md): `flag_device_min_X/Y/Z` | Same thresholds as D–F, for negative values. |
| J–L | Contiguous positive near-limit run, ≥160 samples | [`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs.md): `flag_contiguous_max_X/Y/Z` | Set `min_length = 160`; CDC also assigns the run to every overlapping minute. |
| M–O | Contiguous negative near-limit run, ≥160 samples | [`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs.md): `flag_contiguous_min_X/Y/Z` | Set `min_length = 160`; CDC permits runs to cross minute boundaries. |
| P | Contiguous impossible gravity values | [`acti_flag_impossible()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md): `flag_impossible` | Generalized thresholds are configurable; CDC uses seven samples, \<0.01 g change on each axis, vector magnitude \>1.25 g, excluding ±6 g values. |
| Q | Contiguous adjacent zero values | [`acti_flag_all_zero()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md): `flag_all_zero` | Package checks all three axes. CDC documents a historical programming error that checked only X; exact reproduction of that error is not intended. |
| R | Contiguous identical, non-zero three-axis samples | [`acti_flag_repeated_samples()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_repeated_samples.md): `flag_repeated_samples` | Configure `min_length = 2`, `exclude_zero = TRUE`, `require_equal_axes = TRUE`. CDC’s reported run length/minute attribution may differ. |
| S–U | Axis-specific 1-second spike counts | `acti_flag_spike_second(by_axis = TRUE)`: `flag_spike_second_X/Y/Z` | Set `window_seconds = 1`, `min_spikes = 13`, `spike_size = 11`; CDC counts qualifying local-extremum events. |
| V | Minute before and after an invalid minute | [`acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods.md): `flag_adjacent_invalid` | Caller supplies invalid periods; CDC’s hour-boundary exception requires matching group boundaries. |
| W–Y | Axis-specific interval jumps within a second | `acti_flag_interval_jump(by_axis = TRUE)`: `flag_interval_jump_X/Y/Z` | Set `window_seconds = 1`, `min_repeats = 10`, `min_distinct = 3`, `min_separation = 0.5`; implementation is an approximation of the CDC interval-jump rule. |

Letter labels are made from columns already present in the data; the
helper does not run detectors or infer missing axis-specific results:

``` r

raw <- acti_flag_spike(raw, by_axis = TRUE)
raw <- acti_flag_device_limit_windows(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                      min_count = 690)
raw <- acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                              min_length = 160)
raw <- acti_flag_cdc_labels(raw)
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`acti_day_index()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_day_index.md)
  : Calculate a Baseline-Relative Activity-Day Index

- [`acti_day_start()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_day_start.md)
  : Find the Start of an Activity Day

- [`acti_fill_zeros()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_fill_zeros.md)
  [`acti_fill_zeroes()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_fill_zeros.md)
  [`acti_remove_leading_zeros()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_fill_zeros.md)
  [`acti_remove_leading_zeroes()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_fill_zeros.md)
  : Fill in Zeros

- [`acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods.md)
  : Flag periods adjacent to invalid periods

- [`acti_flag_cdc_labels()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_cdc_labels.md)
  : Label quality flags with CDC NHANES letters

- [`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs.md)
  [`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limits()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs.md)
  : Flag contiguous device-limit runs

- [`acti_flag_device_limit_windows()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_device_limit_windows.md)
  : Flag device-limit counts within time windows

- [`acti_flag_qc()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_qc.md)
  [`acti_flag_qc_all()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_qc.md)
  : Flag Quality Control Values

- [`acti_flag_repeated_samples()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_repeated_samples.md)
  : Flag repeated samples

- [`acti_flag_spike()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_interval_jump()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_spike_second()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_device_limit()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_adjacent_device_limit_samples()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_same_value()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_all_zero()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  [`acti_flag_impossible()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_flag_spike.md)
  : Flag Spikes

- [`acti_hms_to_minute()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_hms_to_minute.md)
  : Convert an HMS Time to a Minute Index

- [`acti_minute_to_hms()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_minute_to_hms.md)
  : Convert a Minute Index to an HMS Time

- [`acti_raw_data`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_raw_data.md)
  : Example Actigraphy/Activity Raw Data

- [`acti_repeat_time_of_day()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_repeat_time_of_day.md)
  : Repeat a Time of Day Across a Recording

- [`acti_resample()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_resample.md)
  [`acti_resample_to_time()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_resample.md)
  : Resample 3-axial input signal to a specific sampling rate

- [`acti_separate_time()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_separate_time.md)
  [`acti_separate_times()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_separate_time.md)

- [`acti_tidy_axes()`](https://jhuwit.github.io/actibase/reference/acti_tidy_axes.md)

  Is the object of class `AccData`
